newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-ISDA reports sharp rise in derivatives trade.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-ISDA reports sharp rise in derivatives trade.

text.p: The International Swaps and Derivatives Association (ISDA) said on Wednesday that premliminary indications suggest that combined global interest rate and currency swaps and interest rate options transactions grew 37.1 percent in calendar 1996.
Outstanding contracts for these type of privately negotiated derivatives stood at US$24.292 trillion at end-1996, compared with US$17.713 trillion a year earlier.
ISDA released the prelimary figures at its annual conference, currently being held in Sydney.
ISDA said that the indicated difference for the second half of 1996, when outstandings stood at US$21.069 trillion, was US$3.223 trillion or 15.3 percent.
Tom Montag, co-chairman of ISDA's market survey committee and a partner at Goldman Sachs, said the final figures could show some adjustment from the data released today.
The data, which is compiled by Arthur Anderson accounting firm from data provided by ISDA members, should be complete in the Northern Hemisphere's spring.
The statistics include new business activity as well as the unexpired contracts that remain outstanding.

ISDA is an international organisation whose membership comprises more than 300 of the world's largest commercial, merchant and investment banks, corporations, government entities and other institutions.
ISDA's members represent a broad cross section of the institutions that act as dealers and end-users of swaps and other privately negotiated derivatives transactions worldwide.
